subject: [PATCH 2/2] mm/memcg: migrate per-node hugetlb lruvec stat together with hugetlb folio

reviews.author: Joshua Hahn
reviews.summary: Identified a potential issue with accessing obj_cgroup_memcg requiring an RCU lock due to Qi Zheng's series.

reviews.author: Oscar Salvador (SUSE)
reviews.summary: Clarified the need for an RCU lock to access obj_cgroup_memcg, but expressed uncertainty about mod_memcg_lruvec_state() calls.

reviews.author: Muchun Song
reviews.summary: Confirmed the need for an RCU lock to ensure liveness of lruvec, which is accessed through memcg.
reviews.raw_body:
> On Sep 22, 2026, at 12:30, Oscar Salvador (SUSE) <osalvador@kernel.org> wrote:
> 
> On Mon, Sep 21, 2026 at 09:20:53PM -0700, Joshua Hahn wrote:
>> On Tue, 22 Sep 2026 06:15:07 +0200 "Oscar Salvador (SUSE)" <osalvador@kernel.org> wrote:
> 
>>> Why do we need the whole thing to be embraced by rcu?
>> 
>> Hi Oscar,
> 
> Hi Joshua,
> 
>> 
>> I believe it's because now getting the memcg from the objcg requires
>> an RCU lock to make sure it doesn't get removed while we work on the
>> memcg. I think this is since Qi Zheng's "Eliminate Dying Memory
>> Cgroup" series.
> 
> Yes, I understood that obj_cgroup_memcg might need the rcu-dance, but I was
> unsure about the mod_memcg_lruvec_state() calls.

The caller needs to make sure the liveness of lruvec, in which case,
lruvec is from memcg, so rcu lock is needed here.

Thanks,
Muchun

> 
> 
> -- 
> Oscar Salvador
> SUSE Labs

2026-09-22.patch_summary: The patch aims to migrate per-node hugetlb lruvec stats together with hugetlb folio, but there are concerns about the RCU lock required for obj_cgroup_memcg.
